text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: Each token contributed returns only 0.75 to me but 3 total to the group, so keeping everything is individually dominant yet contributing all 20 maximizes collective payoff. Since this repeats over 10 rounds, I'll start cooperatively by contributing the full 20 to signal good faith.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 0.75 to each of 4 members, meaning 3 total value per token but only 0.75 back to the contributor—so keeping tokens is individually dominant while contributing all is group-optimal. I'm weighing some partial cooperation to encourage reciprocity rather than pure self-interest.

I'll settle on contributing 10 as a reasonable signaling move without fully committing to either extreme.
